prompt: A student podcaster asks twelve friends, 'Isn't my new intro much clearer than the old one?' All twelve say yes, yet her listening figures show most new listeners stop within the first minute. Why is the survey result mostly noise, and what should she weight more?

options.text: The question was leading and the sample was friendly and unrepresentative, so the drop-off behaviour of actual new listeners is the stronger evidence to act on
Twelve people is too small a sample for any survey, so she should ask fifty more friends the same question
Friends are always dishonest about creative work, so she should never ask anyone she knows anything
Listening figures are unreliable, so the unanimous survey should override them

explanation: A leading question pushes people towards one answer, and friends are not the audience whose behaviour matters here. What new listeners actually do — stopping in the first minute — is less flattering but far more informative.
